frequency_question: How often do highly motivated sovereign states succeed in establishing domestic production lines for advanced foreign cruise missiles or equivalent precision-guided munitions during an active conflict within a two-to-three year timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign nations in active total war attempting technology transfer and domestic manufacture of foreign-designed long-range missiles; excludes peacetime defense procurement or domestic designs built from scratch.

cases.name: Soviet Union replication of German V-2 technology (TsKB-1) 1945-1947
Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile series domestic production transition 1970s-1980s
Iran replication and production of Chinese/North Korean cruise/ballistic systems 1990s-2000s
Pakistan domestic production of transferred ballistic missile technology (Shaheen series) 1990s

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 4 named; estimated 5 total historical programs matching severe existential wartime urgency and advanced missile tech transfer.
known_gaps: Historical classification of clandestine missile programs limits complete enumeration of failed attempts.
skeleton: 4 successful historical precedents of sovereign adaptation under urgency divided by estimated total comparable historical attempts (approx 5)
validity_reason: The base rate depends on modern industrial manufacturing and technology transfer dynamics which remain stable through the medium term.
